chunks: What Ishaq ibn 'Ammar narrated from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام concerning:

Regarding a man who finds a mouse in his vessel, after having performed wudu (ablution) from that vessel many times, washed his clothes from it, and performed ghusl from it, while the mouse had become decomposed: he said, if he had seen it in the vessel before performing ghusl, or performing wudu (ablution), or washing his clothes, and then did that after seeing it in the vessel, then he must wash his clothes, wash everything that that water touched, and repeat the wudu (ablution) and the salat (prayer). But if he only saw it after he had finished all of that and done it, then he should not touch any of the water, and there is nothing upon him, because he does not know when it fell into it. Then he said: perhaps it only fell into it at that very time when he saw it.

key_terms.إِنَائِهِ: his vessel or container holding the water in question
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the salat (prayer) that must be repeated in some cases
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: the ritual wudu (ablution) that must be repeated in some cases
key_terms.سَقَطَ: fell into the water, referring to the uncertain time of contamination
key_terms.فَأْرَةً: a mouse found in the vessel, causing concern about najasah
key_terms.مُتَفَسِّخَةً: decomposed, indicating a dead body in an advanced state

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone finds a dead mouse in water he already used for wudu (ablution), ghusl, and washing clothes?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about water found to be contaminated by a decomposed mouse. If the person knew of the impurity before using the water, he must wash affected items and repeat wudu (ablution) and salat (prayer); if he discovered it only afterward, nothing is due because the time of contamination is unknown.
